import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Recurrence $a(n) = (a(n-1) + a(n-2)) \pmod n$

$a(0) = a(1) = 1$; $a(n) = (a(n-1) + a(n-2)) \pmod n$.

*References:*
- [A096535](https://oeis.org/A096535)-/

namespace OeisA96535

/-- Recurrence $a(n) = (a(n-1) + a(n-2)) \pmod n$. -/
def a : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0 => 1
  | 1 => 1
  | n + 2 => (a (n + 1) + a n) % (n + 2)

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 1 := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 1 := by rfl

/--
All numbers appear infinitely often, i.e., for every number $k \ge 0$ and every frequency $f > 0$
there is an index $i$ such that $a(i) = k$ is the $f$-th occurrence of $k$ in the sequence.
- _Klaus Brockhaus_, Aug 29 2006
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (k : ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ∃ i : ℕ, i > N ∧ a i = k := by
  sorry

end OeisA96535

reformulations.difference: Lean requires an occurrence of each k beyond every index bound N, whereas OEIS conjecture (1) describes the existence of the f-th occurrence of each k for every positive integer f.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each k, its occurrence indices form a subset of ℕ. Being unbounded is equivalent to being infinite, which ensures that every positive-numbered occurrence exists. Conversely, for any bound N, the (N+2)-th occurrence must have index i with i+1 ≥ N+2, hence i > N. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, proved the full universally quantified ↔, encoding an f-th occurrence precisely as a i = k ∧ Nat.count (fun j => a j = k) (i+1) = f. The proof does not use the admitted conjecture and has no sorry dependency.
